requirement:
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`. Each obligation maps to at least one test with assertions on the outcome.

I did not read implementation source. I judged only from the supplied test text. The state-root resolution rules belong to the cited `requirements.configuration.state_location`, so I did not reassess them.

**Per-run record location and identity**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[usage_record_identifies_its_run_and_unusable_state_is_reported]` runs the CLI and checks that exactly one file exists under `<state>/habeas/authoring/usage/`. The file is named `<run_id>.json`.
- The same test asserts `version`, `run_id`, canonical `project_root`, `subject`, `subject_kind`, `backend`, `model`, `evidence_output == "file"`, and that `start_time_ms` is positive and no later than `end_time_ms`.
- A second `--force` run leaves the first record byte-identical and adds a second file, so each assessment gets its own record.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_reviews_are_confirmed_with_fresh_targeted_conversations]` and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[adaptive_routes_fresh_assessments_and_records_each_model]` check that run ids differ between records.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[confirm_runs_a_second_assessment_with_its_own_usage_record]` and the batch tests check that each assessment has its own record.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[usage_subject_kind_is_known_before_sources_are_prepared]` covers the four subject kinds (requirement, example, citation review, site review). It also covers an unknown subject.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[usage_record_of_an_early_failure_identifies_its_subject_kind]` checks the kind on a run that fails before sources are prepared.

**Determination kind, outcome, evidence_written, and evidence_output**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` runs `true`, `false`, and `FIXME` in stdout mode. It asserts `determination` equals the kind, `evidence_output == "stdout"`, `evidence_written == true`, and `outcome == "completed"`.
- File mode is covered by `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]`, which asserts `FIXME` and `evidence_written == true`. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]` asserts `false`. The batch tests assert completed with `evidence_written == true`.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence]` covers failed runs in both destinations. It asserts `failed`, `evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`, `evidence_written == false`, and a null determination.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[failed_evidence_write_keeps_the_accepted_judgment_in_usage]` covers a failed write after an accepted judgment. It keeps `determination == "FIXME"`, sets `evidence_written == false`, and records outcome `failed`.

**Usage stays outside the project in stdout mode**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[usage_state_inside_the_project_is_refused_before_creating_it]` points the state at a directory inside the project. It runs both file and `--stdout` modes and asserts failure with the "must be outside the project repository" message. It also asserts that no directory was created and that the evidence is unchanged.
- The stdout test checks that the usage file is written at the path reported on stderr.

**Failed, cancelled, and unfinished runs are distinguishable**
- `src/authoring/usage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cancelled_request_persists_elapsed_time_and_incomplete_totals]` asserts that a fresh record is `unfinished` with null `end_time_ms`. After `finish("cancelled")` the record is `cancelled` with an end time.
- Failed runs are asserted in the batch, submission, and early-failure tests. Completed runs are asserted as `completed`.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure]` counts one `failed` and five `completed` records.

**No source text, prompts, responses, rationale, or FIXME entry text**
- `src/authoring/usage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[input_metadata_counts_components_and_reads_without_persisting_source]` asserts that the serialized record contains none of the private source, requirement, term, builtin, file, item, or match strings.
- `src/authoring/usage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tool_outcomes_are_distinct_and_unknown_names_do_not_leak_model_text]` asserts that model-supplied tool names are not stored.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts that the usage JSON lacks the requirement text, definition text, source payload, rationale, auth key, and the FIXME entry `#125`.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` asserts that the usage record lacks the literal API key.

**State-location failure**
`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[usage_record_identifies_its_run_and_unusable_state_is_reported]` covers an unusable state location. A state path blocked by a file, and an unset state path with no `HOME`, both fail with a nonempty stderr. They write no stdout and leave the evidence preserved.

**Residual gaps**
There is no explicit assertion that `backend` and `model` are absent when unknown. The requirement only says "when known", and the early-failure test does exercise that path. I do not treat this as a gap.

Habeas MUST store persistent per-user activity state under
`$XDG_STATE_HOME/habeas` on Unix when XDG_STATE_HOME is an absolute, nonempty path,
otherwise under `$HOME/.local/state/habeas`. On Windows it MUST use
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/habeas/state`. `HOME` and `LOCALAPPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. Features MUST use a named subdirectory under that
state root and document their record formats and locations.
State MUST persist across invocations and MUST NOT be stored in the project
repository, the configuration file, or a disposable cache directory. Habeas MUST
create the required directories when recording state. If it cannot determine or
write the state location, the operation requiring that state MUST report the
failure and MUST NOT claim that its history was recorded.
